evidence.intree_statement: Definition iprod_ump {C : Category} {A : Type} (f : A → C) (L : Limit (DiscreteCat_Functor f)) (c : C) (pi : ∀ a, c ~> f a) : ∃! u : c ~> iprod f L, ∀ a, iprod_proj f L a ∘ u ≈ pi a.   -- the A-indexed product of the family f, with iprod f L := vertex_obj[L] and iprod_proj the limit legs

Class HasIndexedProducts (C : Category) := { indexed_product {A : Type} (f : A → C) : C; indexed_product_proj {A : Type} (f : A → C) (a : A) : indexed_product f ~> f a; indexed_product_ump {A : Type} (f : A → C) : IsIndexedProduct f (indexed_product f) (indexed_product_proj f) }

statement_record.book: Specializing Sigma_! and Pi_! along the unique map ! : X → 1 recovers the coproduct and the product of the indexed family (A_x): Sigma_{x in X} A_x is the DEPENDENT SUM, its elements the dependent pairs (x0, a0) with a0 in A_{x0}; Pi_{x in X} A_x is the DEPENDENT PRODUCT, its elements the dependent functions f with f(x) in A_x.
statement_record.intree: iprod_ump / IsIndexedProduct / HasIndexedProducts: the A-indexed product of a family f : A → C as the limit of DiscreteCat_Functor f, with the universal property ∃! u : c ~> iprod f L, ∀ a, iprod_proj f L a ∘ u ≈ pi a.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in three ways: the PRODUCT half only (there is no indexed-coproduct counterpart anywhere in the tree, hence no dependent sum); it is an abstract limit in an arbitrary category, never connected to Pi_! along a terminal map (no slice adjoints exist at all); and it has NO instance — grep finds no HasIndexedProducts instance in the library — so the element-level readings 'dependent function' and 'dependent pair' are never computed in Sets or Coq.
